cases.name: order-then-id
cases.claim: points follow `order` ascending; a tie on order goes by id

cases.name: no-order-at-all
cases.claim: a Zone whose Markers carry no `order` reads them by id

cases.name: missing-order-after-ordered
cases.claim: a Marker without `order` comes after every ordered one

cases.name: order-not-whole-reads-missing
cases.claim: an `order` that is a string, a fraction or a boolean reads as missing

cases.name: repeated-corner-kept
cases.claim: a repeated point stays in the outline as written

cases.name: shape-values
cases.claim: `polygon` and `line` as written; absent, empty, another case or any other value read `polygon`

cases.name: zone-on-two-maps
cases.claim: one outline per Map the Zone has Markers on, by map id

cases.name: dangling-markers
cases.claim: a Marker whose `zone` or `map` is not served is counted `dangling`, placed nowhere

cases.name: zone-without-markers
cases.claim: a Zone with no Marker has no outline and is counted `no_markers`

cases.name: z-present-and-absent
cases.claim: `z` as written; absent or not a whole number reads 0

cases.name: z-above-depth-kept
cases.claim: a `z` past the Map's `depth` is kept as written; a reader reports, never fixes

cases.name: no-point
cases.claim: a Marker or Pin without a whole `x` and `y` is left out, counted `no_point`

cases.name: pins
cases.claim: a Pin's point and its element as the wire's two ids; none, or only one, reads both null; an unserved element keeps its ids

cases.name: pin-without-a-served-map
cases.claim: a Pin whose `map` is not served, or absent, is counted `no_map`

cases.name: map-without-width
cases.claim: a missing `width` or `height` is the largest x or y of the Map's own outlines and Pins, with `extent: points`

cases.name: scale
cases.claim: `scale` is the Map's `x_metres_per_pixel` when a positive number, else null; `length_unit` is never a scale

cases.name: hidden-zone-as-owner
cases.claim: the owner is served the hidden Zone and its Markers: its outline is read like any other

cases.name: hidden-zone-as-visitor
cases.claim: a visitor is served neither: no outline, and nothing in `out` names it

cases.name: code-point-order
cases.claim: zones and pins sort by id in code point order, never by UTF-16 unit

cases.name: whole-by-value
cases.claim: a whole number is read by value: 2.0 is 2, as x, z, order and width

cases.name: row-without-id-ignored
cases.claim: a row with no string id is no element: ignored, never counted

cases.name: last-row-wins-pin
cases.claim: two Pin rows with one id: the last served is the Pin, its point and its element

cases.name: last-row-wins-marker
cases.claim: two Marker rows with one id: the last served is the Marker, in its own Zone and order

cases.name: last-row-wins-map-and-zone
cases.claim: two Map rows and two Zone rows with one id each: the last served of each is read

cases.name: last-row-wins-when-it-reads-less
cases.claim: the last row wins though it is unplaced or names no served map: never the last that reads

cases.name: measured-frame-from-placed-points
cases.claim: a measured width or height reads only placed points: a dangling or unplaced point measures nothing

cases.name: z-not-whole-reads-0
cases.claim: a `z` that is a string, a fraction or null reads 0 and the point stays placed; `2.0` is 2

cases.name: no-placed-marker
cases.claim: a Zone whose Markers are all unplaced or dangling is counted `no_markers`, each Marker under its own reason

cases.name: marker-dangling-before-no-point
cases.claim: a Marker both dangling and without a point counts once, as `dangling`

cases.name: pin-no-map-before-no-point
cases.claim: a Pin with neither a served map nor a point counts once, as `no_map`

cases.name: type-and-shape-case-exact
cases.claim: `type` and `shape` are read as written: `Map`, `Zone`, `Marker` and `PIN` are none of the four, `Line` is a polygon

cases.name: plan-airlock
cases.claim: the plan of record's airlock: four corners in order, its outside door's Pin with its Object

cases.name: plan-forge
cases.claim: the plan of record's forge: nine corners, three of them one point, kept as written

cases.name: plan-of-record-whole
cases.claim: the whole ship, 304 elements as the owner is served them (the plan of record at its git 21ebeda: z an elevation, 0 on every Marker, a room's height in x_height_m)

elements.name: the Halcyon
elements.description: The place aboard: the ship's inside.

elements.name: the Halcyon
elements.description: The vehicle: the ship as a thing.

layout_cases.name: layout-absent
layout_cases.claim: a Map with no `x_layout` is no layout map: a marked Pin on it is in no `hand`

layout_cases.name: layout-null
layout_cases.claim: `x_layout` null is no layout

layout_cases.name: layout-a-string
layout_cases.claim: `x_layout` that is not an object is no layout, even when the string is a method's name

layout_cases.name: layout-without-method
layout_cases.claim: an object without `method` is no layout, and its ground is not read

layout_cases.name: layout-method-empty
layout_cases.claim: a `method` of `""` is no layout

layout_cases.name: layout-method-not-a-string
layout_cases.claim: a `method` that is not a string is no layout: no ground is read, and no Pin is in `hand`

layout_cases.name: board-every-pin-is-hand
layout_cases.claim: on a board (`method` `"hand"`) every Pin of the Map is in `hand`, marked or not; a Pin whose element is not served is still a Pin

layout_cases.name: only-true-is-the-mark
layout_cases.claim: on a layout map of a known method, only `x_hand` exactly `true` puts a Pin in `hand`: `"true"`, `1`, `false` and absent read as placed by the method

layout_cases.name: pin-of-a-hidden-element
layout_cases.claim: a Pin served with its element link null (its element hidden from this reader) is still a Pin: marked on a layout map, it is in `hand`

layout_cases.name: unknown-method-answers-itself
layout_cases.claim: a method string no page names is a layout map all the same: `layout` is the string, and its marked Pins are in `hand`

layout_cases.name: ground-served
layout_cases.claim: a ground naming a served Map answers its id; its size is not returned (the served Map's own `width` and `height` win, and the caller holds it); a Pin on the ground Map is not this Map's

layout_cases.name: ground-not-served
layout_cases.claim: a ground naming a Map the reader is not served is no ground

layout_cases.name: ground-without-map
layout_cases.claim: a ground with no `map` is no ground

layout_cases.name: ground-is-the-layout-map
layout_cases.claim: a ground whose `map` is the layout Map itself is no ground

layout_cases.name: plain-map-keeps-its-marks
layout_cases.claim: a Map whose `x_layout` was removed reads plain: its Pins keep `x_hand: true`, and the mark means nothing there

layout_cases.name: map-gains-a-method
layout_cases.claim: a Map with three Pins placed by hand gains a method: the writer marks all three before it writes `x_layout`, so a new lay-out keeps all three

layout_cases.name: hand-in-id-order
layout_cases.claim: `hand` is by id in code point order whatever order the Pins are held in; a marked Pin on another Map is not this Map's

layout_cases.name: hand-in-code-point-order
layout_cases.claim: `hand` is by id in code point order, never by UTF-16 unit: an id holding a character above U+FFFF sorts after one holding U+FFFF, though its first UTF-16 unit is lower

layout_cases.name: repeated-pin-id-last-row-wins
layout_cases.claim: two rows with one Pin id are one Pin, and the last row served is the one read (reading I): a Pin marked in its first row and not in its last is not in `hand`, and one unmarked in its first row and marked in its last is

layout_cases.name: pin-without-a-string-id
layout_cases.claim: a Pin row with no id, and one whose id is a number, is no Pin (reading H): neither is in `hand`, and the reading does not fail on them

layout_cases.name: map-without-a-string-id
layout_cases.claim: a Map row with no `id`, and one whose `id` is a number, is no Map (reading H): the reading answers `layout` and `ground` null and `hand` empty for either, whatever the row carries and whichever marked Pins are held, one with no `map` and one whose `map` is the number among them
